question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 10 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that an elementary matrix is obtained by performing exactly one elementary row operation on the identity matrix $I.$

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices. 

- The matrix $A$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from $I$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=-8{R}_{1},$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-8{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =A\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from $I$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $C$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from $I$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+10{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 10 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are elementary matrices.
